reason: Attacked and held, with one honest softness named below. I could not open a Pantheon or Faber 1952 Dru volume: every Internet Archive copy of the Dru translation (leisurerhebasiso0001alex, leisurebasisofcu00piep, leisurebasisofcu0000unse, leisurebasisofcu0000jose) is a lending item and returns HTTP 403 on its djvu text, and both search engines I tried outside the exhausted WebSearch budget answered with a CAPTCHA, which I did not attempt. So wordingChecked is false: I did not put my own eyes on Dru's page. What I did establish. (1) The cited article does carry the sentence verbatim as proposed, colon and all, and cites it precisely as 'Josef Pieper, Leisure The Basis of Culture (Translated by Alexander Dru with an Introduction by T.S. Eliot. New York: Pantheon Books, 1952, pp. 40-41)', with the title carrying no comma, which is the note's claim. (2) I downloaded and read the whole 1998 Malsbary translation (archive.org item leisure-the-basis-of-culture-1998-josef-pieper-gerald-malsbary). Its parallel sentence reads 'Leisure is a form of that stillness that is the necessary preparation for accepting reality; only the person who is still can hear, and whoever is not still, cannot hear.' Structurally identical, verbally nothing like it, which vindicates the note's insistence that the translator be named: this is a line that cannot ship untranslated-attributed. (3) That parallel falls at line 2043 of the Malsbary file, inside the title essay's chapter III, which runs from line 1837 to line 2265, and it sits near the start of that chapter. It is preceded there by 'leisure as ”non-activity” - an inner absence of preoccupation, a calm, an ability to let things go, to be quiet', the counterpart of the Dru sentence the evidence quotes about an attitude of non-activity, of inward calm, of silence. So ch. III of the title essay is well grounded, and pp. 40 to 41 in a Pantheon volume whose title essay runs from roughly p. 19 to p. 73 in five chapters is arithmetically where chapter III opens. Nothing contradicts the citation. shipped.js: no match, no near match, Pieper at 0 of 3, not banned. Not in the misattribution list; no speaker question, it is Pieper's own prose, not a quotation inside it. In scope: Musse und Kult 1948, Dru 1952, well before 1999, philosophy and not scripture, nothing needing a warning. Source line leads with the name, carries no dash, and is 110 characters. Perfect for a month of stillness and silence. THE SOFTNESS, which the editor should know: 'pp. 40 to 41' comes from a block citation covering two separated excerpts, so it is the range for the block, not a page pin for this one sentence, which on the Malsbary evidence sits at the start of chapter III and is therefore most likely p. 41. Tag Philosophy is right for Pieper even though the source line calls it 'the title essay'. I offer a tightened source line below, but the proposal as it stands is not false.
betterCitation: Josef Pieper, Leisure the Basis of Culture, the title essay, ch. III, p. 41 (trans. Alexander Dru, 1952)
